properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued April 20 at 1:50PM CDT until April 20 at 5:00PM CDT by NWS Austin/San Antonio TX
properties.description:
Northeastern Bexar County in south central Texas...
  Southeastern Comal County in south central Texas...
  West Central Guadalupe County in south central Texas...

* Until 500 PM CDT.

* At 150 PM CDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated 
  thunderstorms producing heavy rain across the warned area. Between 
  1 and 3 inches of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 
  1 to 2 inches are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is 
  ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

  HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms
           producing flash flooding.

  SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

  IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
           urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
  San Antonio, New Braunfels, Schertz, Cibolo, Converse, Universal 
  City, Live Oak, Selma, Randolph AFB, San Antonio Int Airport, 
  Kirby, Alamo Heights, Windcrest, Terrell Hills, Bulverde, Garden 
  Ridge, Shavano Park, Hollywood Park, McQueeney and Olmos Park.

Caution should be used particularly during the afternoon/evening 
commute.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood 
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Stay away or be swept away. River banks and culverts can become 
unstable and unsafe.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued April 20 at 5:57PM CDT until April 20 at 9:00PM CDT by NWS Austin/San Antonio TX
properties.description:
Northeastern Bexar County in south central Texas...
  Southeastern Comal County in south central Texas...
  West Central Guadalupe County in south central Texas...

* Until 900 PM CDT.

* At 557 PM CDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated 
  heavy rain across the northeast and central parts of Bexar County 
  and northern Guadalupe County. Between 2 and 4 inches of rain have 
  fallen the past three hours. Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 
  inches are possible in the affected areas within the next 2 to 3 
  hours. Flash flooding is ongoing according to webcams and reports.

  HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding.

  SOURCE...Radar and rain gauges.

  IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
           urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
  San Antonio, New Braunfels, Schertz, Seguin, Cibolo, Converse, 
  Universal City, Live Oak, Selma, Randolph AFB, San Antonio Int 
  Airport, Canyon Lake, Kirby, Alamo Heights, Windcrest, Terrell 
  Hills, Bulverde, Garden Ridge, Shavano Park and Hollywood Park.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood 
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the 
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Stay away or be swept away. River banks and culverts can become 
unstable and unsafe.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law 
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National 
Weather Service when you can do so safely.
